rounds.text: SRG Housing Finance Ltd demonstrates exceptional historical compounding, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 35% and a 10-year compounded profit growth of 33% [E14, E18]. This robust operating momentum persists with recent trailing twelve-month sales and profit growth both hitting 29% and 33% respectively [E17, E21], backed by a rules-based screen score of 82 out of 100 yielding a BUY rating with medium confidence [E59]. Valuation multiples appear highly attractive, with the stock trading at a P/E of 14.9x [E1] and a P/B of 1.63x [E2], representing a distinct discount to sector benchmarks of 19.65x and 2.12x [E6, E7]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 536 per share against the current market price of Rs 308, offering a substantial margin of safety of 42.5% [E39, E40], while the reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in a mere 4.4% earnings growth compared to the 12.0% base case [E41]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -247 Cr for Mar 2026 [E31] and the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4].

Despite reported profits, SRG Housing Finance Ltd is burning cash at an alarming rate, posting a devastating negative operating cash flow of Rs -247 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -249 Cr in March 2026, which pushes cash conversion down to an alarming -7.72x [E30, E31, E32]. This severe liquidity mismatch is compounded by official flags highlighting a low interest coverage ratio and a low return on equity of 12.2% over the last three years [E56, E57]. Furthermore, insiders are heading for the exits as promoter holding has dropped significantly by 8.81 percentage points from 67.83% in September 2023 to 59.02% in June 2026, while domestic institutional holdings have been entirely wiped out to 0.00% [E35, E37, E58]. Compounded share price growth over the past year has stagnated at -1%, and the company refuses to reward shareholders, offering a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting profits [E4, E25, E55]. Conceded: the company trades at a reasonable P/E of 14.9x with robust long-term sales growth and sits comfortably above its moving averages [E1, E14, E44].

However, this rapid headline expansion coincides with catastrophic cash burn, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -247 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -7.72x in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Conceded: the P/E of 14.35x and EV/EBITDA of 10.74x sit below sector benchmarks [E6, E11], but these lower multiples are entirely justified by a low return on equity of 10.94% lagging the sector benchmark of 12.5% [E9], a low interest coverage ratio [E56], and a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Finally, while a DCF model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 536 [E39], it completely ignores the negative free cash flow of Rs -249 Cr [E32] and the stagnant share price performance yielding -1% over one year [E25] and -2.7% over twelve months [E46].
